Full body harness, lanyard, and anchor points inspected and used.
Ladder inspected, set at a 4:1 angle, secured, and extends 1m above the roof.
Mark and cover fragile roof areas, skylights, and asbestos zones with safety boards or mesh.
Ensure roof edge guardrails are at least 1.1m high, or set up warning lines 2m from the edge.
Monitor weather: wind below 20 km/h, temperature, and lightning warnings.
Lock and tag all switchgear, isolators, and central inverters with a multi-lock box, and verify with the client.
Verify dead circuits using a Live-Dead-Live test with a calibrated high-voltage tester before starting work.
Restrict substation entry, use rubber insulation mats, keep ventilation running, and maintain required safety clearances.
Isolate inverters and use a thermal camera to check DC combiner boxes for hot spots.
Clean inverter fans, filters, and heat sinks, and confirm DC busbar torque marks are intact.
Record DC string polarity and Voc, and ensure insulation resistance passes the Megger test.
Check that earth grid and lightning protection system (LPS) conductors have low resistance (<10 Ohm).
Secure heavy cable trays, ground metallic channels, and seal wall openings with fire stops.
Store chemicals, coolants, and cleaning agents safely with Safety Data Sheets (SDS) available on site.
Evacuation point identified, alarm system tested, and emergency plan shared with everyone.
Ensure all fire extinguishers, hose reels, and fire suppression systems are clear and easy to reach.
Certified first aid present on site with an accessible eyewash station and trauma kit.
Wear hearing protection in high-noise areas like transformer, generator, or compressor rooms.
Separate electronic waste, broken solar cells, and hazardous materials for licensed disposal.
Remove temporary grounds and locks, sign off the work permit, and clean up the site.
